title: Occupational groups total
rationale: This entry represents the aggregate of all occupational groups, not a single occupation. The score reflects an average exposure across the entire labor market, acknowledging that AI's impact varies widely from minimal for highly physical jobs to very high for digital knowledge work. Many sectors are experiencing significant reshaping due to AI's ability to automate tasks and enhance productivity.

title: 0  Armed forces (Level 1)
rationale: The core functions of armed forces involve significant physical presence, combat, and real-time human decision-making in unpredictable environments. While AI can assist with intelligence, logistics, and operate some autonomous systems, it does not fundamentally automate or replace the need for human personnel in frontline roles or leadership. The work remains predominantly physical and interpersonal, with AI playing a supportive rather than transformative role in core tasks.

title: 01 Commissioned armed forces officers (Level 2)
rationale: The core duties of armed forces officers involve leadership, strategic decision-making, and direct command in unpredictable physical environments. While AI can assist with intelligence analysis and logistics, it cannot replace the essential human element of leadership, real-time presence, and interpersonal command in the field.

title: 011 Commissioned armed forces officers (Level 3)
rationale: Commissioned armed forces officers perform a significant mix of knowledge work, such as strategic planning, intelligence analysis, and logistics, where AI can offer substantial assistance. However, the core of the role involves critical human leadership, ethical decision-making under pressure, and physical presence in unpredictable operational environments, which are less susceptible to AI automation. This blend places it in the moderate exposure category.

title: 0110. Commissioned armed forces officers (Level 5)
rationale: Commissioned officers require significant human leadership, physical presence, and real-time decision-making in unpredictable environments. While AI can assist with intelligence analysis, logistics, and strategic planning, it cannot replace the core human elements of command, ethical judgment, and interpersonal leadership in the field.

title: 02 Non-commissioned armed forces officers (Level 2)
rationale: The core duties of a non-commissioned armed forces officer involve leadership, physical presence, and real-time decision-making in unpredictable, often dangerous, environments. While AI can assist with intelligence, logistics, or administrative tasks, it cannot replace the essential human elements of command, physical interaction, and on-the-ground judgment. The work is predominantly physical and interpersonal, with AI's impact limited to peripheral support.

title: 021 Non-commissioned armed forces officers (Level 3)
rationale: This occupation involves significant physical presence, leadership, and real-time human interaction in unpredictable environments. While AI may assist with logistics or intelligence analysis, it cannot automate the core tasks of commanding personnel, making tactical decisions in the field, or providing human leadership. The work is fundamentally not digital and requires human judgment in complex physical settings.

title: 0210. Non-commissioned armed forces officers (Level 5)
rationale: This occupation primarily involves physical presence, leadership, and real-time human interaction in unpredictable and often dangerous environments. While AI could assist with intelligence analysis, logistics, or training simulations, it cannot automate the core responsibilities of leading personnel, making tactical decisions in the field, or maintaining morale. The work is fundamentally physical and interpersonal.

title: 03 Armed forces occupations, other ranks (Level 2)
rationale: This occupation is almost entirely physical, hands-on, and requires real-time human presence in highly unpredictable and often dangerous environments. The core tasks involve physical combat, tactical operations, and direct human interaction, which are not amenable to AI automation. While AI might assist with high-level intelligence or logistics, it has minimal direct impact on the daily work of other ranks in the armed forces.

title: 031 Armded forces occupations, other ranks (Level 3)
rationale: The core duties of armed forces personnel (other ranks) are inherently physical, involve real-time human interaction, and require presence in unpredictable environments. While AI may assist with peripheral tasks like logistics or intelligence analysis, it has minimal impact on the direct operational and physical tasks central to these roles.

title: 0310. Armed forces occupations, other ranks (Level 5)
rationale: This occupation is almost entirely physical, requiring direct human presence, manual skills, and real-time interaction in unpredictable environments. While AI might assist with logistics or intelligence at higher levels, its impact on the core duties of 'other ranks' is minimal, primarily limited to very peripheral administrative support.

title: 1  Managers (Level 1)
rationale: Managers engage in extensive knowledge work, including planning, analysis, and communication, much of which is digital and can be augmented by AI. While human judgment, leadership, and interpersonal skills remain crucial, AI can significantly enhance productivity in tasks like data analysis, report generation, and strategic support, leading to high exposure.

title: 1111. Legislators (Level 5)
rationale: Legislators engage in significant knowledge work like policy analysis and drafting, where AI can offer meaningful assistance. However, the core of the role involves complex human interaction, negotiation, public speaking, and representation in unpredictable political environments. These critical functions demand nuanced human judgment, empathy, and physical presence, which are difficult for AI to replicate.

title: 11121 Senior central government officials (Level 5)
rationale: This role is predominantly knowledge work, involving extensive policy analysis, strategic planning, and digital communication. While high-level human judgment, political acumen, and interpersonal skills remain crucial, a substantial portion of the work product is digital and highly susceptible to AI augmentation.

title: 11122 Senior district and local government officials and senior officials (Level 5)

title: 1120 Managing directors and chief executives (Level 4)

title: 12 Administrative and commercial managers (Level 2)
